results.summary_before: This project implements a 2x2 matrix multiplier that receives two matrices over UART and transmits the resulting matrix back. It also provides the four result bytes on parallel output pins, and operates with a 100 MHz clock and a 115200 baud UART interface. The design was tested using a USB-UART bridge and documented with example test cases, including notes on overflow for results exceeding 255. The project credits mentorship and was completed as a student project.

results.summary_before: This project is a simple RISC-V processor supporting the RV32E base instruction set plus Zicond and Zbs extensions. It uses two independent SPI memory interfaces for instruction and data storage, and provides 8 GPIO inputs and 8 GPIO outputs. The processor begins execution from address 0x0 and requires external SPI ROM and RAM for operation. A test program is provided that records GPIO inputs and outputs them after a delay to verify functionality.

results.summary_before: This chip implements a reaction time test where a user presses a start button, waits for an LED to light up after a random delay, and then presses a react button as quickly as possible. The reaction time is displayed in milliseconds on a 4-digit 7-segment display, and cumulative times are shown until reset. If the react button is pressed before the LED, an error message is displayed. Silicon testing revealed that the design is broken: the start button does not start the test, reset does not work, and pressing react puts it in an error state, though it worked on an FPGA.
